solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Store work editor rejected, one involved in plot

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the work-and-editor pair is read backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: one being involved in the plot means it is placed inside that word

parts.note: a plot is the story of a novel or film
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A publisher's assistant turns down a manuscript while being caught up in some intrigue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a scheme to be involved in, but it is the storyline; 'rejected' sends the work and editor backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A depository is a warehouse or place where goods are kept, so it is a store.

clue.text: Dubious girl coming out with a roster

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a girl making her coming-out into society
a table is a list or schedule, like a roster

explanation.surface: A doubtful young woman emerges carrying a duty rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' is not an anagram or extraction signal: a debutante 'comes out' at her first society ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Something debatable is open to question, so it is doubtful or dubious.

clue.text: Informal assent by dad to meet cost

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
yup is a casual way of saying yes

explanation.surface: Father casually agrees to settle the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the assent first, but 'by dad' puts PA alongside it, here in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay up is to hand over money owed, that is, to meet the cost.

clue.text: City type to check an overseas currency one's invested

indicators.note: something invested is put into something else, here into the word for checking

parts.note: to scan is to check or examine
the franc is a currency used in France (formerly) and Switzerland
one is gives I + S, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A city sort of person examines a foreign currency in which money has been put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' stands for 'one is', so it gives two letters; 'invested' places the currency phrase inside the checking word, right after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Californian city is described by the demonym formed from its name, a type of city dweller.

clue.text: But atheist finally believed

parts.note: though can mean but, as in 'it was late, though'

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word atheist

explanation.surface: A sceptic who in the end came round to faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' looks like a link word but supplies THOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: To have thought something is to have believed or supposed it.

clue.text: Record of Soviet bureaucracy?

parts.note: red is the colour linked with Soviet communism
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: An archive recording of Soviet officialdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says 'Record of Soviet', so the charade is read in answer order: RED then TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is the idiom for excessive official rules and paperwork.

clue.text: Fringes of severed nets caught a fish

indicators.note: to net is to catch, so the outside letters enclose the next pieces
the fringes of a word are its outside letters, here of severed

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fish is landed after the edges of the nets were cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nets' looks like a noun but is the verb that puts C + A inside S...D.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad is a type of fish, also called horse mackerel.

clue.text: Cooking oil with garlic creates a little smoke

indicators.note: cooking suggests mixing and altering ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Frying oil with garlic produces a bit of smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarillo is a small thin cigar, literally a little thing to smoke.

clue.text: Case of disease seen regularly by doctor

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters
taking letters regularly means every other letter of seen

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as by in dimensions like 3 by 4

explanation.surface: A sign of illness is noticed often by a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here: to doctor an animal is to neuter it.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor a pet is a euphemism for neutering it, which means removing its sexual organs.

clue.text: Pay to enter island held by mutinous characters from Bounty

indicators.note: being held by means the island letter goes inside the rearranged letters
the letters of Bounty rebelling suggests they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mutineers from HMS Bounty pay to land on an island they have seized.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of Bounty give BUYNTO, with I placed after BUY.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy into a scheme or company is to pay for a share in it, gaining entry.

clue.text: Mother declines possible award when the action's over?

definitions.text: possible award when the action's over?

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal such as a horse
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: A mother refuses a prize after the battle is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' is a legal action, a lawsuit, not a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Damages are money a court awards a claimant once a lawsuit ends.

clue.text: Twelve holding calculators when periodic payments due?

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: twelve noon is midday
summers are people or devices that add up sums

explanation.surface: A dozen people keep hold of calculating machines for when instalments fall due.
explanation.walkthrough: Midsummer Day (24 June) is one of the English quarter days, when rents and other quarterly payments traditionally fell due.
explanation.definitionFit: As a quarter day it was a fixed date for settling rents and regular dues, hence a time of payments.

clue.text: Mammal repeatedly hit heads for its refuge

parts.note: to tap is to strike lightly, often over and over

indicators.note: heads are first letters, here of its and refuge

explanation.surface: An animal beaten again and again makes for its shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a hoofed mammal of tropical America and Asia with a short trunk.

clue.text: Haughty pair, one given wrong mark in top event

parts.note: grand can mean haughty or lofty in manner
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cross, X, marks an answer as wrong

explanation.surface: A snooty couple and a third are marked down at a major competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand prix is one of the main races in motor racing, a premier event.

clue.text: Through gritted teeth, accepting one's been fired?

definitions.meaning: putting up with something unpleasant reluctantly and with resolve
read literally, clamping the jaws on a round shot from a gun

explanation.surface: Someone sacked grimly puts up with the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from patients said to clench a bullet in their teeth during surgery; the second reading takes it literally of a fired round, with 'fired' also suggesting being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means facing an unpleasant necessity with stoic resolve, accepting it grimly.

clue.text: Timber producer has post for driver crossing right class of road

indicators.note: the golf peg crossing the R means it straddles and contains that letter

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golfer places the ball on before using a driver
a trunk road is a main road in Britain

explanation.surface: A lumber firm has a signpost for motorists crossing a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' is a golf club, not a motorist. A trunk road is a major British road category.
explanation.definitionFit: The bole of a tree is what yields usable wood, so it produces timber.

clue.text: Revered priest ultimately comforted, having lost heart

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word priest
losing its heart means the middle letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: reassured means comforted or set at ease

explanation.surface: A respected clergyman eventually consoled after becoming discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' drops the central S of REASSURED to leave REASURED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is held dear and cherished, so it is revered.

clue.text: Having drunk limitless wine, ailing emperor's given herbal remedy

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the rearranged letters contain the next piece
ailing means unwell or out of sorts, so the letters are disordered
without its limits means the first and last letters of wine are removed

explanation.surface: A sick ruler, after downing some wine, is prescribed a herbal cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ailing' rearranges the letters of emperor's and given (the apostrophe ignored); 'Having drunk' takes in the core of wine near the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil of this flowering plant is sold as a herbal supplement, so the plant serves as a remedy.

clue.text: Roof would be better were the two sides reversed

indicators.note: the two sides are left and right, so the letters L and R swap places

parts.note: a better is someone who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: A roof that would be improved if its two slopes were switched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a noun, one who bets; 'two sides' means L (left) and R (right), and swapping them in GAMBLER gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambrel is a roof with two slopes on each side, the lower one steeper, as on barns.

clue.text: Unusual perception shown during service break

indicators.note: during means the perception letters come within the service word

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony or service
ESP, extrasensory perception, is perception beyond the usual senses

explanation.surface: A strange insight displayed during a church interval.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short pause or rest, a break from something.

clue.text: Kitty, heading for Altamira, scours series of caves

parts.note: a kitty is a cat

indicators.note: a heading is the first letter, here of Altamira

parts.note: to comb is to scour or search thoroughly

explanation.surface: A cat on its way to Altamira searches through a network of caves.
explanation.walkthrough: Altamira in Spain is famous for its prehistoric cave paintings, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are underground burial chambers linked by tunnels, a series of caves or galleries.

clue.text: Culinary plant with Latin name I recalled

parts.note: cum is the Latin for with

indicators.note: recalled read as called back means the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A cooking herb given a Latin name that I remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' belongs with 'with' to give CUM, not to the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is a plant whose aromatic seeds are used as a spice in cooking.

clue.text: Goes up to deliver a couple of points

parts.note: to rid is to free or deliver someone from something
E and S are two compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Someone climbs in order to hand over a pair of points.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel, as on a horse or bus, so rides is a synonym of goes.

clue.text: Southern US team has to buy it at the borders

indicators.note: the dying word sits at the borders of the team word, surrounding it

parts.note: to buy it is slang for to die
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A sports side has to make a purchase at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buy it' is slang for being killed, not shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixie is a nickname for the states of the American South.

clue.text: More troubled about location of ashes? One might be

definitions.text: More troubled about location of ashes? One might be

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of More are rearranged

parts.note: an urn holds a person's ashes after cremation

explanation.surface: Someone grieving is more upset about where the ashes will rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges MORE into MOER, which goes 'about' URN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person grieving at a funeral would be the one most upset about where the ashes lie.

clue.text: Key worker at home right out of time

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: out of means the time letter is removed from the synonym

parts.note: dexter is heraldic and Latin-derived for right

explanation.surface: An essential worker at home who is out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' suggests an essential employee; here the key is a book's index.
explanation.definitionFit: An indexer compiles a book's index, the key that guides readers to its contents.

clue.text: European family repelled deity

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A European household drove off a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Nike was the Greek goddess of victory, so she is a deity.

clue.text: Artful teacher claims English exercises set back someone not attending fully?

indicators.note: to claim is to take in, so the first pieces surround the next

parts.note: sly means artful or cunning

indicators.note: set back means the exercises letters are reversed

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises at school
a head is a head teacher

explanation.surface: A crafty headmaster claims English exercises have been postponed for an inattentive pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' looks like a delay to the lessons but reverses the school exercises abbreviation; 'claims' places the English pieces just before the last letter of the artful word.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowsy person is only half awake, so is not fully paying attention.
